meaning: Current object storage retains all five generations and offers neither coordinated collection nor generation read leases. This probe records the capability gap. It does not require implicit cleanup without an explicitly selected coordinator.
next_action: Design and implement explicit shared coordination before enabling object collection. Bind collector decisions to current and required generations, reader protection, and concurrent publication. Validate behavior with actual Valkey and Redis services.
constraints: GenerationLeaser promises retained bytes until explicit release. An expiring distributed lock alone cannot satisfy that contract.
An in-flight S3 mutation must remain fenced if coordination is lost. Checking a lock immediately before an S3 write is insufficient.
Do not enable S3-only cleanup. Preserve the non-collecting object store for callers without an explicit coordinator.
The probe proves an absent capability. It does not qualify a coordination protocol or prescribe automatic cleanup.
design_questions_for_implementation: Locate the atomic commit point shared by publication, retirement, and reader protection. A lock check before an S3 operation does not fence a delayed operation.
Assess an explicit coordinated-store mode with authoritative KV descriptors and unique object prefixes per upload attempt. Preserve the existing object mode for callers without coordination.
Prevent an old conditional delete from deleting a later upload of identical bytes with the same S3 ETag.
Preserve the until-release reader contract. Do not reclaim a paused reader through TTL alone. Define fenced recovery for abandoned owners.
Keep optional Valkey dependencies outside the passive root package and preserve its measured dependency guard.
